docs.title: Robotics Internship
docs.text:
Tasks, schedule and deliverables of the robotics internship at the School of Engineering, New Uzbekistan University. You work with the Unitree G1 humanoid and the Go2 quadruped, from simulation and policy training to supervised tests on real hardware.

Schedule and deliverables Junior track Senior track

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Schedule and deliverables

    The four-week plan: every work package with its level, week and the deliverable you hand in.

    Open the schedule

  • Junior track

    Task 1. Turn a human motion into a Unitree G1 motion played in MuJoCo, then make the pretrained walking policy walk in a circle.

    Open Task 1

  • Senior track

    Task 2. Train a Go2 locomotion policy in Isaac Lab, widen the command range and investigate what the change does.

    Open Task 2

docs.title: How work is handed in
docs.text:
1. Do the task in a public GitHub repository of your own.
  2. Push everything the task lists: videos, checkpoints, scripts and a short README or report.
  3. Submit the link to your repository through the Google Form given in the task.

Each task states its own deadline and what a complete submission contains.

Before every session

Confirm the emergency stop combination with every person present, and keep 2 m of clear floor around the equipment at all times.

docs.title: Schedule and deliverables
docs.text: The work is split into packages. Each package has a level (Junior or Senior), the week it belongs to and the deliverable that has to be handed in.

docs.title: Core plan
docs.text: Week Package Level Deliverable 1 Joint-order mapping across URDF / MJCF / Isaac Lab / SDK, with a tested conversion script Junior Table + script everyone imports 1 Shared MuJoCo evaluation harness Junior Script + metric definitions 1–2 Jetson Orin NX bring-up: network, DDS, LowState read, ONNX inference benchmark, base container Senior Working onboard inference + latency numbers 1 Safety protocol and hardware checklist Senior Written procedure, signed off by you 1 RL baseline survey Senior Three candidates, a pick, and a working run of the pick 2 Video → motion: GVHMR vs WHAM (TRAM if the camera moves) Junior Jitter and foot-slide comparison 2 Retargeting: baseline vs PHC / ProtoMotions, including limit and clamping analysis Senior Comparison through the harness 2–3 Deploy the Go2 velocity policy to the real Go2 Senior First hardware milestone 3 Tracking: BeyondMimic, SONIC fine-tune, fast off-policy trainer Senior ×3 Training time, tracking error, robustness 3 Sim-to-sim validation of every policy through the harness Junior Comparison table 4 Gantry tests → supervised floor tests on the G1 Group Videos and logged runs 4 Final comparison report Everyone The full matrix

docs.title: Additional assignments
docs.text: Week Package Level Deliverable 1 Set up the MSI computer: install the right Ubuntu version and set up Isaac Lab Junior Ubuntu on the computer, everything running 1 Research flow matching methods and policies Senior Reproducible code, state-of-the-art models 1 Research motion retargeting methods Junior Description of the methods, with an example of how each one worked 2 Train an RL policy for the G1 (MLP) Senior Result in simulation that passes the requirements 3 Run the learned policy on the real G1; research the sim2real and sim2sim gap Senior Sim2real and sim2sim results; working on the real G1 for the best candidates

docs.title: Part A — Human Motion to Robot
docs.text:
Use UltimateBots Studio to generate a motion for the Unitree G1 robot. You can either upload a short human motion video or describe the motion using a text prompt. Keep the motion under 30 seconds and export it as a LAFAN CSV file.

Then, using the Unitree G1 model from the Unitree RL Gym repository, write a Python script that loads the robot in MuJoCo, plays the generated motion, and renders the result as an MP4 video.

Push to your repository:

  • The rendered robot motion (motion.mp4)
  • The source video or text prompt used
  • The LAFAN motion file (motion.csv)
  • Your Python script and a short README explaining how to reproduce the result

In the README, briefly answer:

  1. How did you determine what the columns in the CSV represent?

docs.title: Part B — Walking Policy
docs.text:
Clone the Unitree RL Gym repository and run the pretrained G1 walking policy using its MuJoCo deployment.

The default policy makes the robot walk forward. Modify the setup so that the robot instead walks in a circle.

Push to your repository:

  • A video of the G1 walking in a circle
  • A short note explaining what you changed and why it produces circular motion

In the note, briefly answer:

  1. What inputs does the policy receive, and where do they come from?
  2. What does the policy output, and how is that converted into joint torques?

docs.title: Submission
docs.text:
Deadline: October 20, 2026

Create a public GitHub repository, push everything listed above to it, and submit the link to the repository through this Google Form.

docs.title: Task 2 — Senior Track
docs.text:
Training a locomotion policy in Isaac Lab, then investigating what a change to the task makes.

If you cannot get Isaac Lab running after a reasonable attempt, fill out this Google Form and explain why it didnt work.

docs.title: Part A — Train a walking policy
docs.text:
Install Isaac Lab by following the official installation guide at https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/

Train the Unitree Go2 quadruped on the flat-terrain velocity tracking task that ships with Isaac Lab. Use the default settings. Training runs headless, without a visualizer, and should take a few minutes.

When training finishes, load your trained policy and watch it run in the Newton visualizer. Record the screen.

Push to your repository:

  • A video of your policy running
  • Your trained checkpoint file

docs.title: Part B — Widen the command range and investigate
docs.text:
During training, the policy is given velocity commands sampled from a range. By default the linear velocity range is roughly minus one to plus one metre per second. Find where this range is set in the configuration and widen it to minus two to plus two.

Before you run the training, write down what you expect to happen and why. Put this in your report. If the result contradicts your prediction, say so and explain what you had wrong. A wrong prediction that is honestly analysed scores higher than a correct one with no reasoning behind it.

Retrain with the wider range, then watch the new policy in the visualizer and record it.

Open TensorBoard and compare your two runs. Look at error_vel_xy, success_rate, and the base contact termination rate.

Then retrain the wide-range configuration again, this time with roughly three times as many training iterations, and compare a third time.

Push to your repository:

  • A video and checkpoint for the wide-range policy
  • A video and checkpoint for the wide-range policy trained longer
  • A short report

In the report, answer:

  1. Your prediction, written before you ran the experiment.
  2. What actually happened, with the metrics to support it.
  3. Did more training iterations fix it? If yes, what does that tell you about the cause? If no, what does that rule out?

docs.title: Submission
docs.text:
Deadline: October 20, 2026

Create a public GitHub repository, push everything listed above to it, and submit the link to the repository through this Google Form.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Training with the default number of parallel environments takes a few minutes. If you run out of memory, reduce it — but be aware that the number of environments and the number of iterations are coupled, because one iteration collects a batch of data across all environments at once. A run with eight times fewer environments sees eight times less data over the same number of iterations.

docs.title: Стажировка по робототехнике
docs.text:
Задания, расписание и результаты стажировки по робототехнике в инженерной школе New Uzbekistan University. Вы работаете с гуманоидом Unitree G1 и четвероногим роботом Go2: от симуляции и обучения политик до тестов на реальном оборудовании под присмотром.

Расписание и результаты Трек Junior Трек Senior

docs.title: С чего начать
docs.text:
• Расписание и результаты

    Четырёхнедельный план: каждый рабочий пакет с уровнем, неделей и результатом, который нужно сдать.

    Открыть расписание

  • Трек Junior

    Задание 1. Превратить движение человека в движение Unitree G1 в MuJoCo, а затем заставить предобученную политику ходьбы идти по кругу.

    Открыть задание 1

  • Трек Senior

    Задание 2. Обучить политику ходьбы Go2 в Isaac Lab, расширить диапазон команд и разобраться, к чему это приводит.

    Открыть задание 2

docs.title: Как сдавать работу
docs.text:
1. Выполните задание в собственном публичном репозитории на GitHub.
  2. Загрузите всё, что перечислено в задании: видео, чекпоинты, скрипты и короткий README или отчёт.
  3. Отправьте ссылку на репозиторий через Google Form, указанную в задании.

В каждом задании указан свой срок и состав полной сдачи.

Перед каждым занятием

Убедитесь, что все присутствующие знают комбинацию аварийной остановки, и держите 2 м свободного пространства вокруг оборудования.
